standard_prerequisites.name: Representable functors
standard_prerequisites.statement: A functor F : Set^(A^op) is representable when there merely exists a : A with a natural isomorphism y a = F, where y is the Yoneda embedding.
standard_prerequisites.use: Clause (ii) of the counted statement is that for each b : B the functor a |-> hom_B(Fa,b) is representable; the definition is retained as context at source lines 991-996.

standard_prerequisites.name: Adjunctions by unit, counit and triangle identities
standard_prerequisites.statement: F : A -> B is a left adjoint when there are G : B -> A, eta : 1_A -> GF, eps : FG -> 1_B satisfying the triangle identities (eps F)(F eta) = 1_F and (G eps)(eta G) = 1_G.
standard_prerequisites.use: Clause (i) of the counted statement is that F is a left adjoint, and the proof reconstructs G, eta and eps from the representing isomorphisms (source lines 1022-1025) and conversely builds the representing family from them (source lines 1028-1039).

standard_prerequisites.name: The Yoneda embedding is an embedding and representability is a mere proposition
standard_prerequisites.statement: By the Yoneda lemma the embedding y : A -> Set^(A^op) is fully faithful, and if A is a category then y_0 is an embedding, so representability of a functor is a mere proposition (book Corollary 9.5.7 and Theorem 9.5.9).
standard_prerequisites.use: Retained as context at source lines 998-1004, where the author records the mere-propositionality of representability that makes clause (ii) a property rather than structure.

core_obligations: Unpack clause (ii): an element of it consists of a function G_0 : B_0 -> A_0 together with, for all a : A and b : B, an isomorphism gamma_{a,b} : hom_B(Fa,b) = hom_A(a,G_0 b) satisfying gamma_{a,b}(g o Ff) = gamma_{a',b}(g) o f for f : hom_A(a,a') (source lines 1018-1020).

From (ii) to (i): set eta_a := gamma_{a,Fa}(1_{Fa}) and eps_b := inverse of gamma_{Gb,b} at 1_{Gb}, define G on hom-sets by G_{b,b'}(g) := gamma_{Gb,b'}(g o eps_b), and check that G is a functor and that eta and eps are natural and satisfy the triangle identities, a verification the author skips because all the statements involved are mere propositions (source lines 1022-1026).

From (i) to (ii): take gamma_{a,b} to be the composite hom_B(Fa,b) -> hom_A(GFa,Gb) -> hom_A(a,Gb) given by G and precomposition with eta_a, with inverse given by F and postcomposition with eps_b; the triangle identities provide the inverse (source lines 1028-1039).

Round trip (ii) -> (i) -> (ii): the object function G_0 is preserved, so only gamma has to be compared; the newly defined gamma sends f to G(f) o eta_a, and rewriting G(f) by its definition and using naturality of gamma gives back the old gamma (source lines 1041-1049).

Round trip (i) -> (ii) -> (i): the functor G is recovered on objects, its action on hom-sets is recovered from G(g o eps_b) o eta_{Gb} = G(g) by functoriality and the triangle identity, and eta and eps are recovered by their defining clauses from the newly built gamma (source lines 1051-1061).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack what an element of the representability clause consists of.
Build G, eta and eps out of the representing isomorphisms.
Build the representing isomorphisms out of an adjunction.
Compare the two composites, first on gamma and then on G, eta and eps.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.5.10 at source lines 1010-1016: a functor F : A -> B is a left adjoint exactly when for every b : B the functor a |-> hom_B(Fa,b) is representable. The 46-line proof builds a quasi-inverse in both directions and then checks two round trips that live in different types, so neither can be waved through. The direction from representability must invent the functor action G(g) := gamma_{Gb,b'}(g o eps_b) together with eta_a := gamma_{a,Fa}(1_{Fa}) and eps_b := inverse gamma_{Gb,b}(1_{Gb}) (lines 1022-1025); the reverse direction must produce the whole family gamma from G and eta with inverse built from F and eps, using the triangle identities (lines 1028-1039). The first round trip is a rewrite of G(f) o eta_a that consumes naturality of gamma (lines 1041-1049), and the second recovers the hom-action of G from G(g o eps_b) o eta_{Gb} = G(g) and then re-derives eta and eps from their defining clauses (lines 1051-1061). The statement records neither the naturality equation that gamma has to satisfy nor the two composites.
